posts.title: Google's November 2026 core update and Gemini 4 Hydrogen: what founders should do
posts.metaTitle: Google's November 2026 core update and Gemini 4 Hydrogen
posts.metaDescription: Google's November 2026 core update and Gemini 4 Hydrogen landed two days apart. What changed, why your data is harder to read and what to do now.
posts.excerpt: Google started its November 2026 core update on 10 November and made Gemini 4 Hydrogen live in Search on 12 November. Here's how to read the overlap without panicking.
posts.heroImageAlt: Two calendar pages for 10 and 12 November pinned to a corkboard, joined by yellow string to a search bar with a question mark
keyPoints: Google started the November 2026 core update on 10 November; its dashboard says the rollout may take up to 2 weeks ([Google Search Status Dashboard](https://status.search.google.com/incidents/WLxcJyC6jMWMfryxsKMc)).

Gemini 4 Hydrogen went live across Search on 12 November; Google calls it "the biggest model upgrade to Search yet" ([Google](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/gemini-4-hydrogen-search-upgrade/)).
Log both dates, wait for the rollout to finish and compare like with like before changing anything.

faqs.q: When did Google's November 2026 core update start?
faqs.a: Google's Search Status Dashboard says it released the November 2026 core update on 10 November. It applies globally and to all languages, and the rollout may take up to 2 weeks to complete.

faqs.q: What is Gemini 4 Hydrogen?
faqs.a: It's Google's new model for Search. Google calls it "the biggest model upgrade to Search yet" and says it is available globally in Google Search for all users.

faqs.q: Why is November search data hard to read?
faqs.a: The core update and Gemini 4 Hydrogen landed two days apart, so a change could come from either. Search Engine Journal notes that, on Google's two-week estimate, the first full week after the rollout has finished would include Black Friday, so compare like with like.

faqs.q: Is Google sending more clicks from AI answers?
faqs.a: Google says it has added more links to its AI experiences, but neither of its posts gives click numbers. Your own Search Console and analytics are the numbers to trust.

posts.title: You can now claim a ChatGPT business profile: what it means for small brands
posts.metaTitle: ChatGPT business profile: what Business Hub means
posts.metaDescription: OpenAI now lets you claim a ChatGPT business profile and see how often you're mentioned. What's live, what's US only and what small brands can do.
posts.excerpt: OpenAI's new Business Hub lets eligible businesses claim a ChatGPT business profile and see mentions and clicks. Here's what's live outside the US, what isn't and what to do first.
posts.heroImageAlt: A hand stamping a tick on one yellow business card in a grid of grey cards
keyPoints: Eligible businesses can claim a ChatGPT business profile in Business Hub (beta) and see mentions, website clicks and discovery topics ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/)).
Business Agents and shopping in ChatGPT are US only for now ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/), [ChatGPT merchants page](https://chatgpt.com/merchants/)).

faqs.q: Can I claim a ChatGPT business profile outside the US?
faqs.a: OpenAI says any eligible business located where ChatGPT is available can claim their business through Business Hub, and that availability depends on the business's location and type. It doesn't list eligible countries or categories. One catch: local stores and restaurants can currently claim only an existing US listing.

faqs.q: Is Business Hub the same as the ChatGPT Business plan?
faqs.a: No. This is not ChatGPT's paid Business plan. OpenAI's help page says you don't need an Ads account or a ChatGPT Enterprise agreement to claim an eligible business.

faqs.q: Does claiming a profile make ChatGPT recommend you more?
faqs.a: OpenAI says it doesn't guarantee increased visibility or give you direct control over ChatGPT's independent recommendations, and that advertising doesn't influence ChatGPT's independent answers.

faqs.q: What do Business Hub mentions count?
faqs.a: For an online business, a mention counts when ChatGPT references its website. Naming the brand alone doesn't count. Insights show aggregate activity over the past 28 days.

posts.title: Google AI Mode ads are scaling in Australia, Canada and Singapore, with the UK planned
posts.metaTitle: Google AI Mode ads: Australia, Canada, Singapore, UK planned
posts.metaDescription: AI Mode ads are scaling in Australia, Canada and Singapore, and Google plans to add the UK in Q4 2026. What changed and what small brands should check now.
posts.excerpt: Google is scaling ads in AI Mode in Australia, Canada and Singapore, and plans to add the UK in Q4 2026. Here's what changed and what to check before you spend.
posts.heroImageAlt: Ad tags hanging on a line, three filled and one dotted outline still to come
keyPoints: Google is scaling ads in AI Mode in 10 new countries, including Australia, Canada and Singapore ([Google, 28 Oct 2026](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ads-in-ai-mode-global/)).
The UK is planned for Q4 2026, not live ([Google](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ads-in-ai-mode-global/)).

Google says existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are automatically eligible, and that paid ads don't influence organic AI responses ([Google Ads Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/18826097)).

faqs.q: Are ads in Google AI Mode live in Australia, Canada and Singapore?
faqs.a: Google said on 28 October 2026 that it is scaling ads in AI Mode in 10 new countries, including Australia, Canada and Singapore.

faqs.q: Are AI Mode ads live in the UK?
faqs.a: Not according to Google. Its 28 October post says it plans to expand to additional locales in Q4 2026, including the United Kingdom. That is a plan, not a launch.

faqs.q: Which Google Ads campaigns can show in AI Mode?
faqs.a: Google's Ads Help page says existing Search, Shopping and Performance Max campaigns are automatically eligible to serve ads within AI Overviews and AI Mode. It also says these ads are available in English in the United States and select English-speaking markets, so check what applies to your own account and market.

faqs.q: Do ads change Google's AI answers?
faqs.a: Google's Ads Help page says paid advertising does not influence the organic responses generated by Google AI.

posts.title: UK rules check: what the CMA and ASA are cracking down on right now
posts.metaTitle: UK rules check: CMA and ASA on reviews, prices and claims
posts.metaDescription: The CMA can now fine firms directly and the ASA uses AI to find misleading ads. What UK small brands need to check on reviews, pricing and green claims.
posts.excerpt: The UK's consumer and advertising regulators have been clear about what they're watching: prices, discounts, reviews, subscriptions and green claims. Here's what they've said, in plain English, and what it means for a small brand.
posts.heroImageAlt: A five-star review card with one star peeling off, beside a price tag with a hidden fee folded underneath
keyPoints: The CMA has opened 20 investigations under its direct enforcement powers and imposed fines of over £11.8 million ([CMA](https://competitionandmarkets.blog.gov.uk/2026/10/14/direct-consumer-enforcement-18-months-on/)).

The CMA says discounts must be genuine and businesses must show the total price clearly. It also says unlawful conduct could include a business requesting members of staff to write reviews ([CMA](https://competitionandmarkets.blog.gov.uk/2026/10/14/direct-consumer-enforcement-18-months-on/)).
The ASA says a 270-character ad still had room to explain a carbon neutral claim ([ASA](https://www.asa.org.uk/rulings/procook-ltd.html)).

faqs.q: Can staff write reviews of their own company's products?
faqs.a: The CMA says commissioning reviews isn't limited to paying consumers, and that unlawful conduct could include a business requesting members of staff to write reviews about its products or services.

faqs.q: What does the CMA expect on prices and discounts?
faqs.a: The CMA says discounts must be genuine and businesses must show the total price clearly and throughout the purchasing journey, without opting customers in by pre-selecting extra services.

faqs.q: When do the new UK subscription rules start?
faqs.a: The CMA says a new subscription contracts regime will come into force in January, and that the government will publish secondary legislation and further guidance ahead of it. The CMA also warns businesses not to assume that its support for compliance means enforcement is being delayed.

faqs.q: Can a short ad skip the basis of a green claim?
faqs.a: Not according to the ASA. In its ProCook ruling it said an ad with a 270-character limit was not so limited that the basis of a carbon neutral claim couldn't be made clear.

posts.title: Consumer trends 2027: what new research means for beauty brands
posts.metaTitle: Consumer trends 2027: trust, proof and outcomes for brands
posts.metaDescription: New 2027 research from Kearney, Euromonitor, Mintel and McKinsey points to trust, proof and outcomes. What it means for small brands, especially beauty.
posts.excerpt: The 2027 consumer trends reports agree on more than you'd expect: beauty is merging with wellness, shoppers want proof over brand names and AI is starting to shape the shortlist. Here's what that means for a small beauty brand.
posts.heroImageAlt: Unbranded skincare dropper, jar, pouch and a candle in a bright flat-lay, with a small bowl and a closed report with a yellow tab
keyPoints: Kearney says consumers are "2x more likely to use beauty for wellness than for self-expression" ([Kearney](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/kearney-releases-2027-beauty-outlook-report-302928612.html)).

Euromonitor's beauty survey says premium buyers choose "premium ingredients over a premium brand by 43% to 18%". The page doesn't say which countries were surveyed ([Euromonitor](https://www.euromonitor.com/voice-of-the-consumer-beauty-survey-2026-key-insights/report)).

Generative AI sways 8% of colour cosmetics purchasers, but only 19% see it as a highly trustworthy source of shopping information ([Euromonitor beauty survey](https://www.euromonitor.com/voice-of-the-consumer-beauty-survey-2026-key-insights/report), [Euromonitor trends](https://www.euromonitor.com/newsroom/press-releases/november-2026/global-consumer-trends-2027)).

faqs.q: What are the main consumer trends for 2027?
faqs.a: The 2027 reports we read point the same way: beauty is merging with wellness, shoppers want proof over a famous name, AI is starting to shape the shortlist and trust still comes from people.

faqs.q: How much does AI influence beauty purchases?
faqs.a: Euromonitor's beauty survey says generative AI already sways 8% of colour cosmetics purchasers and 15% of Beauty Innovators. Its global trends research says only 19% see GenAI as a highly trustworthy source of shopping information.

faqs.q: Do beauty shoppers still buy in store?
faqs.a: McKinsey's Alexis Wolfer says more than two-thirds of beauty sales globally, and about 50 percent in the US, still happen in store.

faqs.q: What do AI tools look for in beauty products?
faqs.a: McKinsey partner Sara Hudson says LLMs pick up on functional words: how something is used, what ingredients are in it and what ingredients are not.
